touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot, plus a direct SEP check across suspend
touch-id.detail: Enrolment and verification work again after a reboot. A pending verify through /dev/sep-bio recovered across two suspend cycles. Suspend with the real lock screen and fprintd has not been tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot
touch-id.detail: Reported to enrol and match after a reboot in SPI mode 2. This comes from a development branch.

thunderbolt.title: Thunderbolt dock: USB, display and resume
thunderbolt.detail: With the final 7.1.12-tbpr8-usb2fix2 build, a TS4 dock's USB2 attached on the first session in 3 of 3 tries, running a keyboard, a mouse and a 3840×2160 display at 120 Hz. Suspend to idle and Ethernet recovery on the TS4 were also reported. Not every dock or role swap was retested.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine driver research (external module)
neural-engine.detail: On J293 the external module only binds. On J316C an encoder inference test matched its reference hash, but SET0 readback is still missing, and the Mac rebooted unexpectedly after a raw debug dump. The proposed kernel was never boot-tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot
touch-id.detail: Matched after each of two separate reboots. With a Thunderbolt display connected, a bring-up retry recovered 2 of 4 boots. This PR did not test J316S.

thunderbolt.title: USB-C and Thunderbolt display, with resume
thunderbolt.detail: An LG UltraFine 5K ran at 3840×2160, 60 Hz and 10-bit from both left-hand ports. Plugging, replugging and a 10-second suspend to idle were tested. The M1 Max path was not tried on hardware.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine driver research (external module)
neural-engine.detail: On J293 the external module only binds. On J316C an encoder inference test matched its reference hash, but SET0 readback is still missing, and the Mac rebooted unexpectedly after a raw debug dump. The proposed kernel was never boot-tested.

touch-id.title: Touch ID after reboot
touch-id.detail: Verified 3 times out of 3 after a reboot, using the commit-3 / test-11.5 work. The earlier enrolment work in #58 went into feat/sep, not the branch that was audited.

neural-engine.title: Neural Engine research (external driver)
neural-engine.detail: Programs ran, but about 1 result in 5 came back all zeros, across three boots, and unloading needed a reboot. It depends on a separate driver and an m1n1 firmware preload; it is not a packaged, supported path.

touch-id.title: Touch ID enrol, verify and sudo through PAM
touch-id.detail: An experimental PR reports this board. The J414C result from #69 does not carry over to J414S, and the separate profile work has not been integrated.

thunderbolt.title: Dual-dock display work
thunderbolt.detail: J414S (draft #46) sits on the review/pr14-base stack and J416C (#50) on the dual-dock branch. Both are development stacks; neither has been qualified on the merged working tree.

thunderbolt.title: USB devices through a Thunderbolt hub
thunderbolt.detail: A USB keyboard worked through an OWC Thunderbolt 5 hub. This does not cover DisplayPort or PCIe tunnelling.

thunderbolt.title: Thunderbolt display and resume work
thunderbolt.detail: This T602x board is the one tested in #8. The code also covers other Pro and Max laptops, but those boards have not been tested.

thunderbolt.title: Dual-dock display work
thunderbolt.detail: J414S (draft #46) sits on the review/pr14-base stack and J416C (#50) on the dual-dock branch. Both are development stacks; neither has been qualified on the merged working tree.

usb.title: USB 3 on every plug, replug and flip
usb.detail: A USB 3.2 Gen 1 stick came up at 5 Gbps in 6 of 6 attaches: each of the three USB-C ports, both cable orientations. The PHY coprocessor is stopped on every unplug and booted again on the next plug, as macOS does. Suspend with a USB 3 device attached, 10 Gbps and DisplayPort alt mode were not tested.

audio.title: Speakers, microphones and headphone jack
audio.detail: Tested by jgoyvaerts on his own J616s: the six speakers through the J616 speaker graph with speaker protection running, the three internal microphones and the headphone output. In Aurora as merged, the microphones and the jack card work, and the speakers stay locked until a speaker protection config for the J616s ships. The headset microphone and the jack across a suspend were not tested.

graphics.title: GPU on the G17 backend with Mesa as G17P
graphics.detail: Tested by jgoyvaerts on his own J616s with per-unit values his boot loader fills in: the M4 Pro GPU (25G83 firmware) drives the desktop, vkmark completes all 13 scenes and glmark2 runs with no GPU recovery or fault. In Aurora as merged, the J616s GPU stays disabled until m1n1 fills in per-chip calibration, and the Mesa side (mesa#55) is still open. Ray tracing is refused on 25G83.

suspend.title: Suspend to idle by lid and menu
suspend.detail: The lid and the menu put the machine into suspend to idle; opening the lid wakes it and the keyboard and trackpad work after resume. The keyboard only wakes the system on real input (#409). Battery drain over a long sleep was not measured.

boot.title: Linux from the SSD through aura, without a host
boot.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g; not merged yet. aura brings up the USB, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth and PCIe hardware itself, reads the kernel, device tree and initramfs from an EFI system partition on the internal SSD and boots Linux with all 12 CPUs, USB, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and both displays. aura is still chainloaded from the installed stage 1 over the USB debug link for this.

usb.title: USB 2 on the back-left and front ports
usb.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy; not merged yet. A keyboard and an RTL8153 USB Ethernet adapter work on the front ports (behind the on-board VL822 hub), a keyboard on the back-left port, at high speed. The loader has to wake the back-left port controller and release the hub reset first. USB 3, the back-middle and back-right ports and Thunderbolt are not supported.

storage.title: Internal SSD
storage.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy; not merged yet. The ANS2 controller with the T8152 register layout: fio reaches 3.8 GiB/s sequential read, 2.9 GiB/s sequential write and 140k IOPS 4K random read on ext4. With the power-off series the SSD reports a clean shutdown on the next boot.

ethernet.title: On-board 10GbE (Realtek RTL8127)
ethernet.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy; not merged yet. TCP runs at 9.4 Gbit/s in both directions at MTU 1500 once the link is retrained to 16 GT/s (from userspace for now). Keeping the read request size at 512 bytes matters for sending: UDP out is 8.9 Gbit/s at 512 and 7.9 at 4096 (five paired runs each). The r8169 transmit changes are a separate pull request (#21).

cpu.title: All CPU performance states
cpu.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy; not merged yet. All twelve cores run every performance state (P/M up to 4.79 GHz, E up to 2.94 GHz) with load-driven governors, after the fix for the WFxT erratum that corrupted data. The SMC leaves the fan at its minimum, so a fan control service is part of the same change; how warm it gets depends on the load: one full 12-core load held the top states at 67 C with the fan at about 2900 RPM, while stress-ng on all 12 cores reaches 82 C with the fan at about 4500 RPM and the 75 C thermal trips throttle the cores.

hdmi.title: HDMI and dual display
hdmi.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy; not merged yet. HDMI through the dptx-phy and the Parade PS190 converter at 2560x1440 next to the USB-C display at 1280x720; Linux gets both as framebuffers. Mode changes after boot and hotplug are not supported.

audio.title: Speaker and headphone jack
audio.detail: Tested by Thomas Glanzmann on his own J873g, booted through the m1n1/aura proxy; not merged yet. Playback works on the headphone jack and on the internal speaker. The speaker stays off unless explicitly enabled, until a speaker protection profile for the J873g exists. The headset microphone was not tested.
